definition: Sedentary means involving much sitting; settled and inactive.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word sedentary. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know sedentary should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Doctors classify long-haul trucking as sedentary work despite the miles: the body sits still while the odometer runs.
Inactive just means not getting much exercise; sedentary is more specific and a shade stronger — the day is actually built around sitting.
Housebound goes beyond sedentary: the sedentary clerk still commutes and runs errands, while a housebound patient rarely passes the front door.
Bedridden goes far beyond sedentary: a sedentary life is built around sitting by habit or by work, while the bedridden patient has no choice left and cannot leave the bed at all.

Desk-bound means kept at a desk by the nature of the work — the job itself pins you to the chair. It describes workers and their posts. Sedentary is wider: it counts all the sitting in a day or a life, at desks, in trucks, on sofas, however it came about.

Stationary means fixed in one place, and it applies to things as readily as to people — a parked truck with the brake set, a weather front that refuses to move. Sedentary belongs to bodies and lifestyles, counting hours spent sitting; a machine can be stationary, but only someone with a chair can be sedentary.

After the concert season moved online, the choir director noticed her days had gone entirely sedentary: podium to piano bench to sofa, four thousand steps on a good day where twelve thousand used to be.
Nothing about her work had gotten easier — only stiller.
Sedentary is the honest word because it measures sitting, not character: it is not lazy.
A surgeon bent over a microscope for ten hours is doing grueling, exacting work and having a perfectly sedentary day — the word counts hours in the chair, not effort.
Sedentary is the health report's word: it counts chair-hours without judging character, so prefer it to lazy when you mean sitting, not shirking.
Its cluster-mate inert belongs to objects and total stillness — a sedentary analyst still types, travels, and talks; an inert machine does nothing at all.

The insurer's annual report used one word for the studio's workforce, and the word was sedentary.
It was not an insult so much as arithmetic: badge data showed the average employee sat for eleven of the twelve hours they spent in the building.
The founders, both former bike messengers, took it personally.
Within a month the studio had walking meetings, standing scrum boards, and a rule that any call under twenty minutes was taken on foot.
